title: Autonomous A/B Integrity Conductor — dynamic thresholds and rollback rationale capture
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build an autonomous A/B integrity conductor that ties automated evals and quality signals to config and model flips, enforces dynamic cohort-level thresholds, and executes a transparent rollback with root-cause tagging. This ticket scopes the controller, signal fusion logic, safety heuristics, and the developer-facing audit trail (why we rolled back). The system should support: 1) multi-metric fusion (quality, latency, hallucination markers), 2) synthetic probe injections for baseline, 3) cohort-aware thresholds that adapt to sample size, and 4) an explainable rollback action that records the decision provenance and links to the failing metric traces.

Initial synthetic probe run shows 0.8% hallucination baseline and 0.5% on candidate variant — we artificially lowered threshold to validate path.

2026-03-11 - QA (Tariq): Runbook drafted with manual verification steps and automatic rollback simulation steps. Found a race condition when two overlapping rollbacks for adjacent cohorts occur. Mitigation: leader-election per-exposure and queued rollback operations with backoff.

2026-03-12 - Asha: Blocker noted — Dedicated autoscaler can change capacity which affects latency signals. Need to pin capacity snapshot or normalize latency by allocated GPU slots. Added dependency on infra ticket INF-1287 to provide stable capacity snapshot API.
Next steps: finalize hysteresis tuning, add Bayesian minimum-sample threshold, complete e2e tests against staging rollout framework, schedule canary exercise with Product for March 22.

Acceptance criteria: (1) Controller executes automated rollback when fused-signal crosses adaptive threshold with confidence >= 95%, (2) Audit entry stored with decision provenance and links to traces/PRs, (3) No more than one rollback per exposure window per cohort, (4) Playbook and Grafana panels exist for SRE & PM troubleshooting.
notes: Design decisions: use Bayesian sample-size adjustment + weighted z-score fusion to handle small cohorts; hysteresis implemented as a dual-window confirmation (fast detect window + slow confirm window); rollback actions are reversible and recorded as signed audit events.

Trade-offs: aggressive thresholds reduce customer exposure time but increase false positive rollbacks for noisy cohorts. We will expose a developer-configurable sensitivity knob that defaults to conservative (low false positives) for enterprise customers.
Rollout plan: start with internal beta using synthetic traffic and 1% live traffic for non-critical routes; monitor for two weeks; then expand to broader A/B experiments with signoff.

Implementation notes: controller will be a new microservice stateless controller w/ durable audit store in existing telemetry DB. Use existing auth scopes for private deployments and include KMS audit hooks per security guidance.
